Singing Voice Synthesis (SVS) represents a specialized subfield of speech synthesis that addresses the intricate demands of human vocalization, including articulation, timbre, and vibrato. While traditional approaches have largely failed to meet the rigorous requirements of SVS, recent advancements in deep learning have catalyzed significant breakthroughs in the field. This article provides a comprehensive survey of current deep learning-based SVS methodologies, examining their underlying principles, specific architectures, and performance outcomes. Furthermore, we identify persistent challenges and propose prospective research avenues for future development.

This paper introduces NIPS4Bplus, an enhanced version of the NIPS4B birdsong dataset, featuring richer annotations and a larger collection of recordings. The updated dataset comprises 1,000 birdsong recordings from 100 distinct species, with 500 of those recordings annotated by a human expert and the remaining 500 by a machine learning system. This new release expands the database to include 2,000 additional recordings from 1,000 birds across 500 species, annotated by a combination of a new machine learning system and a human expert. The dataset is accessible via https://nips4bplus.github.io.

Event cameras are biologically inspired sensors that capture scenes by reporting pixel-wise changes in luminance, resulting in a stream of asynchronous events. Although this design offers significant advantages for dynamic scenes, it necessitates specialized processing techniques. This paper introduces a method to replicate the classic calibration of frame-based cameras, adapted for event-driven data. By utilizing a standard checkerboard, we estimate intrinsic and extrinsic parameters, as well as the distortion coefficients for event cameras. The approach is validated through experiments on both synthetic and real-world datasets.

Graph learning has emerged as a pivotal field in machine learning, offering a robust framework for modeling intricate relationships and patterns within data. Driven by the escalating volume of graph-based datasets across domains like social networks, biological systems, and knowledge graphs, the domain has garnered significant interest from both academia and industry. This survey paper provides a thorough examination of contemporary graph learning methodologies, encompassing both unsupervised and supervised paradigms. It details the underlying principles, primary advantages, and specific use cases for various techniques, while also addressing current limitations and prospective avenues for future research.

We present findings concerning exceptional collections on $\Sigma _{ 2 }$, an Enriques surface characterized by two $(-2)$-curves being contained within a single rational curve. This Enriques surface serves as a quotient of an elliptic curve by a fixed-point-free involution.

This study introduces a method for three-dimensional instrument tracking during retinal surgery, utilizing a spotlight to project a two-dimensional image of the tool onto a camera lens. By integrating this visual input with spotlight data, the system calculates a 3D position for the instrument. This approach is validated through experiments involving a surgical needle, with specific analysis dedicated to the factors influencing tracking accuracy.
This work introduces a recurrence relation for the $F$-polynomials associated with a cluster algebra of finite type, alongside a combinatorial representation based on cluster splitting graphs.

This work examines the viability of a passwordless future powered by FIDO2, focusing on the transition hurdles faced by both users and providers. We argue that while FIDO2 holds the promise of a frictionless, secure future, its success relies on specific advancements. These include expanding the adoption of FIDO2-compatible devices, lowering implementation costs, and enhancing user education. We further explore the critical role of WebAuthn in driving this future and highlight its current limitations. Ultimately, we conclude that although a passwordless future is achievable with FIDO2, it remains contingent upon continued technological innovation and widespread adoption.

This paper examines Weyl-Wigner calculus concerning lattice systems, specifically within the context of the one-dimensional tight-binding model. It is demonstrated that the standard calculus approach yields incorrect results when applied to such lattice models.

This study examines the impact of YouTube's interface design on users' sense of agency, defined as the feeling of having control and influence over one's online environment. Through a controlled experiment involving 100 participants, we compared a custom-built replica of the YouTube mobile app with a standard Android browser. Results indicate that participants using the browser felt greater agency, likely because the search bar placed prominently on every browser page facilitated more direct access to their desired content. Conversely, YouTube positions its channel browsing and search features within distinct areas of the main screen, creating friction that hinders efficient content retrieval. These findings highlight the critical role interface design plays in shaping user agency and offer specific recommendations for improving the YouTube app to ensure smoother access to video material.

This study demonstrates that the $\pi$-calculus possesses a property of behavioural completeness regarding its predicate logic, meaning every definable property is satisfied by a specific subset of its states. This result is established through a construction of a first-order model defined over the transition system, combined with the application of a novel variant of Mostow's theorem. Furthermore, this approach yields a necessary byproduct: the existence of an orbit-finitely executable, orbit-algorithmic model structure for the $\pi$-calculus.

Within the domain of ordered trees, a "neighbor" relationship exists between a tree and any result produced by applying a fundamental operation known as a local move. sPHENIX is a high-energy physics experiment at Brookhaven National Lab's Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider, designed to investigate the properties of strongly coupled quark-gluon plasma. The sPHENIX detector features a solenoidal magnetic field of 0.5 T and a tracking system capable of determining the 3D positions of charged particles with high precision. This tracking system comprises an inner silicon vertex tracker and an outer drift chamber, the latter of which closely resembles the Advanced CTx (ACTS) prototype designed for the future CERN ILD experiment. Consequently, the ACTACTS software developed for this prototype has been adapted and integrated into sPHENIX. This paper details the application of this software to reconstruct tracks within the sPHENIX detector, outlining the reconstruction procedures and analyzing the resulting track quality metrics.

This study examines the evaluation of a jump term arising in the analysis of space-time finite elements for arbitrary temporal interpolation. We demonstrate that this term can be transformed into a sum of lower-dimensional integrals, a result that holds uniformly regardless of the interpolation method used in the temporal direction. Furthermore, the paper establishes that this term can be efficiently and accurately computed by applying a simple weighting to boundary integrals defined on the problem domain.

A signed graph is mono-directed when its positive edges form a connected component. This paper presents a classification of mono-directed signed graphs that admit circular flows. Furthermore, this research establishes that signed graphs with circular flow properties are precisely those whose unoriented counterparts possess circular flow properties as well.

The subset sum problem involves determining whether a specific target can be formed by summing a chosen subset of integers from a given collection. While the deterministic algorithms proposed by Bj\"orklund and Karpinski in 2004 address this problem within $O(n\log_2 n + m)$ time—where $n$ represents the count of input integers and $m$ is the target—our work introduces a novel deterministic method that achieves a superior time complexity of $O((n+m)\log n + m\log _2 n)$.

We introduce a catalog of 1,000 flares from 100 M-dwarf stars, derived from ASAS-SN observations. This dataset includes 100 stars, each exhibiting at least 10 flares, with a combined total of 1,000 flares. The catalog details the stars' photometric and astrometric characteristics, as well as the timing, magnitude, and duration of each flare event. We also provide the light curves for 100 representative flares, with durations ranging from 10 to 100 minutes. The catalog's primary utility is to facilitate the identification of flares occurring in stars that are observable by other telescopes, thereby enabling detailed follow-up studies.

Cell migration is a fundamental process in embryogenesis, yet the mechanisms governing it remain poorly understood. In *Drosophila* embryogenesis, hemocytes traverse the embryo's surface to establish a critical tissue. We tracked the movement of these cells using high-resolution microscopy and found that their trajectories are not random; instead, they follow a non-Markovian pattern characterized by persistent forward motion. This behavior arises from a dynamic interplay between the cells and the underlying epithelium. Specifically, as the epithelium elongates, it pulls the overlying hemocytes, causing them to align preferentially with the direction of tissue expansion. This interaction is further complicated by hemocytes actively reorienting themselves away from neighbors, a process driven by repulsive forces. We developed a computational model that integrates these repulsive forces with epithelial pulling mechanisms to simulate hemocyte dynamics. The model successfully reproduces the observed non-random migration patterns, offering a robust framework for deciphering the complex intercellular forces that drive cell movement during embryogenesis.

This paper introduces a semi-supervised speech recognition framework utilizing a contrastive siamese network. By leveraging a siamese architecture, the method extracts speaker embeddings from a vast pool of unlabeled data, while an adversarial learning component trains a speech decoder using a limited set of labeled speech. Experiments conducted on the LibriSpeech dataset demonstrate that this approach achieves a 30% reduction in word error rate (WER) for 50-hour labeled data compared to a baseline, and a 3% improvement for 1000-hour labeled data.

The newly introduced axial longitudinal structure function, $F_{L}^{A}(x,Q^{2})$, is essential for determining the total inelastic cross-section in the presence of longitudinal virtual photon polarization. This paper investigates the optimal control of linear quadratic systems featuring a hidden Markov chain, where the true transition matrix is unknown. We introduce an adaptive control strategy capable of ensuring almost sure convergence to the optimal performance of the fully observable case. Furthermore, we establish that under specific conditions, this adaptive approach achieves strong consistency.

Active inference serves as a unifying framework for explaining how the brain minimizes uncertainty regarding its actions, perceptions, and sensations. This paper introduces a novel computational architecture for active inference grounded in branching time, capable of modeling multiple prospective futures and integrating diverse sensory modalities. The study examines the critical role of temporal abstraction in active inference, revealing that it enables agents to evaluate future events at varying levels of granularity. Additionally, we explore the integration of multi-modal data, demonstrating that the model can seamlessly combine visual and proprioceptive inputs to guide behavior. Finally, we analyze the implications of these findings for the brain, suggesting that this framework may offer a robust computational basis for understanding the neural mechanisms of decision-making.

We establish that for any Baire locally convex space $X$, the following are equivalent: (i) $X$ is Eberlein-Grothendieck; (ii) there exists a Baire locally convex space $Y$ and a continuous surjection $Y \to X$ where $Y$ is Eberlein-Grothendieck; (iii) there exists a continuous surjection $f: Y \to X$ where $f$ is a Baire one function mapping from an Eberlein-Grothendieck space $Y$; (iv) there exists a Baire one mapping $f: Y \to X$ where $f$ is a continuous surjection originating from an Eberlein-Grothendieck space $Y$; (v) there exists a Baire one mapping $f: Y \to X$ where $f$ is a continuous surjection originating from an Eberlein-Grothendieck space $Y$ that is also a weakly continuous map.

The concept of isochronicity is generalized for a class of one-parameter families of Hamiltonian systems within 1D phase spaces, where the property applies specifically to energy level containing closed orbits. Based on the assumption that a neighborhood of these iso-periodic orbits exists, we derive necessary conditions linking the Hamiltonian to the radial component of this neighborhood. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these necessary conditions are also sufficient for isochronous behavior. Finally, we examine a collection of Hamiltonian systems that exhibit this isochronic property.

This study introduces a novel method for analyzing attractor structures within the Lorenz system, utilizing similarity signature curves (SSCs) to identify the creation of periodic orbits. SSCs are generated by tracking the evolution of similarity measures between a reference trajectory and a target one. The analysis reveals that these curves exhibit distinct features corresponding to specific dynamical events, such as the emergence of periodic orbits and the approach toward a system's attractor. The proposed method is validated through numerical simulations of the Lorenz system, where the calculated SSCs align with theoretical expectations.

This paper investigates the Local Asymptotic Normality (LAN) property for distributions arising from a stochastic differential equation (SDE) driven by a Lévy process, where coefficients are subject to small perturbations. By employing the Girsanov transformation adapted for both martingales and processes with jumps, the authors derive necessary conditions to establish that the resulting family of distributions satisfies the LAN property.

We examine the spectrum arising from Laplacians acting on twisted 1-forms within certain hyperbolic manifolds. Our demonstration shows that the spectral values can be expressed through the Teichmüller representation. Furthermore, we provide a concrete example of a compact manifold that exhibits a spectrum which is rationally dependent on the coefficients of a specific Fuchsian group. In addition to this, we address the spectral isospectrality issue concerning the twisted Laplacians of a surface.

We introduce FNetAR, a new framework for causal language modeling that combines causal autoregressive tokens with FNet, a transformer-free architecture utilizing global frequency convolutions. By autoregressively training FNet on causal tokens, FNetAR achieves a superior balance of training efficiency and performance compared to existing methods. Our approach surpasses current state-of-the-art results on standard benchmarks, including GLUE, SuperGLUE, HellaSwag, and RACE, while also demonstrating strong capabilities on domain adaptation and outperforming other transformer-free models on image classification tasks. Notably, FNetAR delivers these gains with a significantly smaller model size, offering a more cost-effective solution for both training and inference.

This study examines the cosmological evolution of generalized ghost pilgrim dark energy (GGPDE) within the Saez-Ballester gravitation framework. By employing the equation of state $p = -\rho^{\pm 1/\alpha}$, we analyze the resulting cosmological models. Our findings indicate that the early universe undergoes a decelerated expansion phase, whereas the late universe transitions to accelerated expansion. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the late universe's acceleration is contingent upon the parameter $\alpha$.

This study examines a multi-agent Mean-Field Game (MFG) involving Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) users, where each user must decide on the placement of Service Function Chaining (SFC) chains across various MEC servers. These users aim to minimize the sum of service quality loss and the cost associated with SFC placement. The authors demonstrate that the corresponding MFG possesses a unique Nash equilibrium. Furthermore, an innovative approach combining Reinforcement Learning (RL) is introduced to determine optimal placement strategies, utilizing a novel reward function that aligns with the game-theoretic framework. The RL algorithm is shown to converge to this unique Nash equilibrium. Finally, numerical experiments confirm the effectiveness of the proposed RL method and the existence of the Nash equilibrium.

We examine a (1+1)-dimensional Dirac fermion model featuring a random mass term, which serves as a prototype for the Anderson insulator in one dimension. Our findings reveal that, under strong coupling, the system flows to a regime where the mass term becomes effectively irrelevant. This indicates that, in the strong coupling limit, the model exhibits a delocalized phase, thereby contradicting the conventional picture of a localized Anderson insulator at strong coupling.

Although depression is a chronic condition, individuals are not constantly depressed; they also experience moments of happiness. However, the majority of research has focused on negative emotions, leaving the nature of positive experiences in depressed individuals largely unexplored. This study investigates the types of happy moments that occur in people with depression, the factors that trigger them, and the emotions felt during these times. We conducted an online survey with 100 participants who each recalled and described their most joyful event over the past year. The results revealed that the most frequently reported happy moments involved social interactions, particularly with family and friends. The factors contributing to these moments included the joy of sharing happiness with others, the satisfaction of having a purpose, and the relief of a temporary remission from depression. Furthermore, the participants reported feeling a mix of joy and sadness while reflecting on these events. The study concludes that while individuals with depression do experience happiness, these moments are often less intense and short-lived compared to those without the condition.

We examine the Sp(4) gauge theory coupled to two mass-degenerate fermions and one massless fermion, which models the light quarks in QCD. Utilizing a novel lattice formulation, we compute the ratio of the massless fermion's mass to that of the massive fermion near the chiral phase transition. Our findings indicate that the ratio is approximately 0.1, a value that aligns well with the isospin symmetry breaking observed in real QCD.

We report on the synthesis and structural characterization of Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_6$, a novel nickel tellurate featuring $S$ = 1 chains. This material exhibits a zigzag antiferromagnetic ordering with a transition temperature ($T_N$) of 10.5 K. Theoretical analysis of the Ni$^{2+}$ spins within the chains indicates that this magnetic order arises from a competition between the nearest-neighbor Heisenberg exchange interaction and a Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interaction. Furthermore, the compound displays a broad specific heat anomaly at $T_N$, accompanied by a pronounced low-temperature tail. The observed width of this anomaly is attributed to compositional inhomogeneity, while the tail is explained by the presence of NiO clusters.

Smart vehicular networks are poised to transform the future of transportation by leveraging advanced technologies to enhance safety, efficiency, and sustainability. However, the integration of these systems introduces significant security and privacy challenges, primarily driven by the inherent volatility of vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs) and the inherent uncertainty in estimating trust levels among communicating vehicles. To address these issues, this paper introduces a trust management framework designed for smart vehicular environments. The proposed solution employs a novel trust evaluation model that incorporates a fuzzy logic approach to manage uncertainty, alongside a specific trust management model tailored for on-board vehicular units. Furthermore, the study outlines a communication protocol for disseminating vehicle trust data and presents a comprehensive framework that incorporates a specific trust evaluation model that leverages fuzzy logic to handle uncertainty, alongside a specific trust management model tailored for on-board vehicular units. This paper investigates monotone cubic spline interpolation applied to functions exhibiting a strong gradient. The central result establishes that, provided the grid is sufficiently fine, the resulting interpolant maintains monotonicity.

This paper investigates Taub-NUT spacetimes within a scalar-tensor framework featuring a hyperbolic nonlinear sigma model, which encompasses Einstein-Maxwell theories with nonlinear photon potentials as specific instances. We derive the exact AdS-Taub-NUT solution for this AdS scalar-tensor setup and analyze its asymptotic behavior. Furthermore, we demonstrate that exact AdS black bounces possessing scalar hair can be formulated in this theory, and we examine the properties of these bounces and their associated linearized quasi-normal modes.

The growing prevalence of sound-based applications has heightened the necessity for extensive sound databases. However, manually annotating these databases is labor-intensive, and the lack of suitable tools makes the process even more arduous. This paper introduces a method designed to mitigate the workload of manual annotation for sound databases by utilizing a large taxonomy. The proposed approach breaks down the annotation task into two distinct phases: first, annotators categorize audio clips within the taxonomy, and second, they refine these selections by adding or removing specific tags. The study evaluates this method through experiments involving a dataset of environmental sounds using the EcoSound taxonomy. Results indicate that this two-stage strategy significantly reduces the time required for manual annotation compared to traditional methods.

This study introduces a novel approach for analyzing the dynamics of complex systems, termed dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT). By applying DMFT to a broad spectrum of nonlinear systems, we demonstrate that their dynamics can be approximated as a linear process occurring within an effective, time-dependent medium. This framework yields analytical solutions for diverse scenarios, including the Lotka-Volterra equations, the Lotka-Volterra-Sir model, and the SIR model. Furthermore, we extend this theory to investigate the stability of ecosystems and the dynamics of chemical reaction networks.
We examine the distribution of avalanche sizes within a single site-occupancy model on a Cayley tree, demonstrating that the resulting distribution is non-uniform.

Discourse comprehension involves understanding the relationships between sentences. This paper introduces a data-driven approach to representing these connections by identifying shared information across sentences. We utilize a question answering framework, where each query is formulated to retrieve the shared content linking a pair of sentences. We further present a comprehensive dataset of such question pairs, which we use to train and assess models. Experimental results demonstrate that this method effectively captures the essence of sentence connections and exhibits strong generalization capabilities.

This review examines the application of Perfectly Matched Layers (PMLs) to hyperbolic wave equations, with a specific focus on the PML-CNC (Complex Changed Coordinates) approach. The article begins by outlining the fundamental principles of PMLs, followed by an analysis of the PML-CNC method. It details the implementation of PML-CNC for both time-dependent and frequency-domain wave equations, along with a comparative assessment of its performance against other PML types. Furthermore, the text explores the integration of PML-CNC with numerical schemes, covering the Finite Difference Time Domain (FDTD) method, the Finite Element Method (FEM), and the Discontinuous Galerkin (DG) method.

This study investigates the deformation and fragmentation of droplets induced by laser pulses, examining how these effects vary with pulse duration, energy, and droplet size. The research reveals that the droplet's response is governed by the intensity of the laser pulse, specifically the ratio of pulse energy to its duration. When subjected to these laser pulses, the droplets exhibit a two-stage evolution: an initial expansion phase followed by a contraction phase. Notably, droplets with a diameter of 1.5 mm display a distinct deformation and fragmentation behavior, characterized by a critical pulse energy threshold.

We present ALMA observations of the LkH$\alpha\,330$ protoplanetary disk, revealing a prominent, narrow ring of millimeter-sized dust grains at a radius of 100 au. This feature is accompanied by a broader ring of carbon monoxide (CO) gas spanning 150 to 250 au. We propose that the millimeter-sized dust ring forms via the dynamical trapping of dust in the gravitational potential well of a protoplanet. This hypothesis is supported by the detection of a 30 au wide ring of carbon monoxide isotopologue $^{13}$CO at 160 au, which aligns with the expected location of a dust-trapping resonance. The spatial separation between the millimeter-sized dust and CO rings suggests that the planet is efficient at clearing gas but ineffective regarding dust, a behavior consistent with a planet of approximately 10 Earth masses. Furthermore, the presence of a distinct ring of submillimeter-sized (micron-sized) grains at 130 au indicates that the planet also traps these smaller particles at a different resonance. Collectively, these findings suggest that the LkH$\alpha\,330$ system is a protoplanetary disk in the process of forming planets.

This paper introduces a novel concept of vector-valued distance applicable to an extensive range of mathematical structures, including metric spaces, quasimetric spaces, and $R$-spaces. We establish fundamental properties of this new metric and examine the associated norm, while also defining and analyzing its specific behavior within the space of symmetric positive definite (SPD) matrices. Furthermore, we apply these insights to develop a specific instance of a generalized calculus, termed gyrocalculus, designed for operations on the manifold of SPD matrices.

Hydrogen is a critical component in Europe's transition toward a sustainable, low-carbon future. This study examines the economic viability of a European hydrogen infrastructure, specifically evaluating the trade-offs between transport costs and the value of decarbonization. We develop a comprehensive model of the European hydrogen network, which is then integrated into the leading global energy market simulator, PLEXOS. Our analysis reveals that a European hydrogen network can significantly lower the overall cost of achieving climate objectives, with a notable positive impact on the northern regions. Furthermore, we demonstrate that hydrogen networks offer greater benefits when used in conjunction with other low-carbon technologies, such as power-to-hydrogen conversion and direct electrification.

Travel-time anisotropy in the solar interior serves as a crucial indicator of the magnetic field's strength and orientation. This study investigates how anisotropy in acoustic wave travel times influences the horizontal magnetic field within the solar convection zone. We developed a 3D magnetohydrodynamic model featuring a stable stratification with a magnetic field that varies linearly in strength along the horizontal axis. The resulting acoustic waves exhibit a travel-time anisotropy that correlates with the magnitude of the horizontal field. We demonstrate that this anisotropy can be identified through the application of a slowness vector inversion technique. The inversion process utilizes the observed travel-time asymmetries to recover the underlying magnetic field's strength. We further assess the method's robustness against noise and variations in the field's spatial profile. Ultimately, this research establishes a viable method for probing the magnetic field in the solar convection zone using solar p-mode helioseismology.

Squeezed light serves as a vital resource for quantum metrology and computing, yet its generation is highly sensitive to imperfections. This study demonstrates that squeezed light produced by a topologically protected photonic circuit exhibits robustness against fabrication errors and component loss. By leveraging the topological invariant of the underlying lattice structure, the researchers engineered a squeezed-light generator that maintains its integrity despite significant deviations in design parameters. Notably, the system achieves up to 97% transmission efficiency for squeezed modes even when the fabrication error reaches 10% of the design scale. Furthermore, the generated squeezed state is entirely immune to loss within the topologically protected channel. These findings establish a new pathway for topologically protected quantum photonic devices, offering substantial potential for advancing quantum information processing and sensing technologies.

This study addresses time-optimal control for a quadrotor drone, aiming to minimize flight duration while adhering to physical constraints. The approach utilizes a double convexification technique to resolve the resulting non-convex optimization problem. The resulting trajectory is formulated as a spline, with coefficients determined by solving a linear program. The paper details the specific physical constraints applied, including limits on total travel time, velocity, acceleration, and jerk. Additionally, it outlines the mathematical derivations for both the convexification process and the calculation of spline coefficients. The authors demonstrate the method's efficacy through several numerical examples, including drone flight paths and spline representations.

This paper investigates the algebraic structure of additive F_{q^2}-conjucyclic codes within the finite field F_q. It introduces a specific mapping that establishes an isomorphism between these codes and a specific class of linear codes over F_q. Leveraging this isomorphism, the study determines the algebraic structure of the aforementioned codes and identifies the conditions under which they form two-sided ideals within the corresponding quotient ring. Furthermore, the paper examines the corresponding quotient ring's algebraic properties, demonstrating that it constitutes a Frobenius ring.

The Topical Group on Career Pipelines and Development (CommF2) outlines a strategic framework for the US High-Energy Physics community, focusing on pathways for entry into the field and long-term professional advancement. This document details key themes, including the recruitment of underrepresented groups, the retention of early-career researchers, and the integration of diverse, inclusive, and equitable practices throughout these career trajectories.

This study reports on the measurement of the $W$ boson polarisation in $t\bar{t}$ events, utilizing a dataset of 20.3 fb$^{-1}$ of proton-proton collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 8$ TeV recorded by the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The analysis focuses on the $W$ boson originating from the quark with the highest transverse momentum in the $t\bar{t}$ pair, specifically within the $e\mu$ decay channel. The observed polarisation is determined to be $0.66 \pm 0.08$ (stat.) $\pm$ 0.04 (syst.), which aligns with the Standard Model prediction of $0.67 \pm 0.04$ (syst.).

This study revisits the light-cone distribution amplitude (LCDA) of the $D$-meson, concentrating on the longitudinal twist-2 and 3 components. By employing the QCD sum rule method, we determine the LCDA parameters, including the leading moment $f_D \langle \xi \rangle$ and the non-leading moments $f_D \langle \xi \chi \rangle$ and $f_D \langle \xi \Delta \chi \rangle$. Our results indicate that the leading moment $f_D \langle \xi \chi \rangle$ is negative, while the non-leading moments $f_D \langle \xi \chi \rangle$ and $f_D \langle \xi \Delta \chi \rangle$ are positive. Additionally, we calculate the LCDA parameters for the non-vanishing twist-3 DA, including the leading moment $f_D^{(3)}$ and the non-leading moment $f_D^{(3)} \langle \xi \chi \rangle$.

The concept of a power hypergraph originates from a graph $G$, where edges are formed by the Cartesian product of vertex pairs $(u,v)$ for each $uv \in E(G)$. This paper introduces the power hypergraph's tensor and defines its eigenvalues, subsequently deriving its characteristic polynomial and calculating the total count of such eigenvalues. Additionally, we explore the relationship between a signed signed subgraph's eigenvalues and those of its underlying graph.

This study examines the potential for cooperative localisation within the Starlink satellite constellation, focusing on how relative position and velocity uncertainties influence a network of $N$ nodes. The analysis assumes a network operating in a Kalmán filter environment with Gaussian noise characteristics. Specifically, the position uncertainty of each node is modeled as a function of the position uncertainty of the node's immediate predecessor in the chain. The paper derives closed-form expressions for the position uncertainty of the $n$-th node, valid for all $n$ ranging from 1 to $N$. These derived bounds are then compared against the actual uncertainties to assess their tightness. Additionally, the study investigates how the position uncertainty of the first node propagates through the chain to affect subsequent nodes.

We report the detection of transit timing variations (TTVs) in the hot Jupiter XO-3b, which manifest as deviations from a strictly periodic transit schedule. These variations are linked to the planet's eccentricity, which is constrained to $e = 0.09 \pm 0.03$ (68\% confidence). The observed TTVs align with tidal evolution models that account for the planet's migration from a high-eccentricity orbit to a circular configuration. The results indicate that the planet's eccentricity has decayed by a factor of at least 10 since the initial formation of the system. Furthermore, the analysis yields a tidal quality factor of $Q \geq 1.1 \times 10^5$ for XO-3b, assuming a tidal Love number of $k_2 = 0.5$.

The 21-cm global experiment seeks to detect the 21-cm signal from the Epoch of Reionization (EoR) by observing neutral hydrogen. However, this signal is overwhelmed by system noise, necessitating precise calibration. Current methods typically rely on estimating the system temperature and noise correlation matrix using the power spectra of the entire time series, but this approach suffers from significant uncertainties due to the long duration of the data. This study proposes a new Bayesian noise calibration method that utilizes the noise wave technique to calibrate the data. By applying this method to the Murchison Widefield Array (MWA) data, we demonstrate that it effectively mitigates the impact of system noise on the EoR signal.

This paper examines the genus $0$ equivariant Gromov-Witten theory of the projective bundle $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E})$ over a compact K\"ahler manifold $X$, where $\mathcal{E}$ is a vector bundle. We demonstrate that the genus $0$ equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants for $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E})$ can be explicitly computed in terms of those of $X$. Furthermore, we investigate a specific class of invariants termed "equivariant Gromov-Witten invariants of type A," which are derived from the standard invariants by applying the Abel map to equivariant moduli spaces of stable maps. We prove that these type A invariants for $\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E})$ are also expressible using a similar type of invariant defined on $X$.
We establish prime number theorems that are uniform across a broad range, which is significantly larger than any previously documented in the literature.

This paper introduces a statistical methodology designed to evaluate treatment efficacy in Alzheimer's disease clinical trials, specifically focusing on the ADAPT dataset. By modeling natural cubic splines within a linear mixed-effects framework, the approach estimates treatment effects at specific time points. To address the resulting high-dimensional inference challenges, we employ a new multiple testing correction method based on the concept of "local false discovery rate." This strategy allows for the estimation of treatment effects across numerous time points while rigorously controlling error rates.

The surge in urbanization and population growth has led to a significant rise in private vehicle usage, creating a severe shortage of parking spaces in cities. This scarcity results in drivers spending considerable time and fuel searching for available spots, causing traffic congestion and environmental degradation. To address this, we introduce CRAWLING, a crowdsourcing algorithm designed to optimize parking space discovery. The system leverages data from connected vehicles to identify parking locations and guide drivers toward them. We present a comprehensive evaluation of the algorithm's performance, analyzing its impact on parking time, fuel consumption, and environmental emissions. The study concludes that CRAWLING effectively reduces parking time by 10% to 20% and cuts fuel consumption and emissions by 5% to 10%.

The effectiveness of flat-minima optimizers in generalizing is well-documented, yet the specific conditions under which they surpass standard training methods remain unclear. This paper addresses this gap by analyzing the performance of flat-minima strategies specifically within the context of overparameterized linear regression. We demonstrate that these optimizers can achieve superior generalization compared to conventional techniques, but only if the loss landscape contains a solitary minimum flat region. Conversely, we identify scenarios where flat-minima approaches underperform. To address these limitations, we introduce a hybrid optimization strategy that combines the flat-minima optimizer with standard training methods. Experimental results indicate that this combined approach consistently outperforms both individual techniques across various scenarios.

This paper introduces a new architecture for reflective Frequency Selective Limiters (FSLs) designed to operate in the 2.4 GHz band. Unlike traditional FSLs that absorb and dissipate the energy of overdriving signals, this reflective design redirects such energy, thereby reducing power loss during high-power events. The system utilizes a parametric amplifier configuration, where a 2.4 GHz signal is applied to a 50-ohm load via a 2.4 GHz/11 GHz bandpass filter. Simultaneously, a 26.5 GHz pump tone is applied to the filter's 11 GHz passband, creating a 13 GHz image signal that mixes with the 2.4 GHz input. This process generates an image signal at 15.5 GHz, which is then amplified by the parametric action of the 26.5 GHz pump. The resulting amplified image signal combines with the original 2.4 GHz input at the output port, creating a 15.5 GHz/2.4 GHz diplexer. Under normal low-power conditions, the 2.4 GHz signal passes through with minimal attenuation. However, when the 2.4 GHz input exceeds the 11 GHz/2.65 GHz mixing threshold, the generated 15.5 GHz image signal is amplified by the parametric action, effectively suppressing the 2.4 GHz signal at the output. This study examines a SEIRS epidemiological model for COVID-19, specifically addressing the extreme scenario where acquired immunity does not exist. In this context, individuals transition from Susceptible to Infected, then to Removed, and back to Susceptible. The analysis focuses on the model's basic reproduction number, denoted as $R_0$, and its associated reproductive threshold. We demonstrate that the system possesses a disease-free equilibrium, which is locally asymptotically stable whenever $R_0 < 1$. Furthermore, when $R_0 > 1$, a unique, globally stable endemic equilibrium emerges. These findings are substantiated by numerical simulations.

Word embeddings are a cornerstone of modern natural language processing, yet selecting the appropriate model for a specific task remains a critical challenge. This paper introduces a new method for evaluating and choosing word embeddings by leveraging the intrinsic quality of their contextual information. We demonstrate that context quality can be assessed by analyzing how well a word's neighbors align with its neighbors in a learned word-neighborhood space. This approach yields a straightforward, computationally efficient metric that is highly effective at predicting task performance. We apply this method to three distinct NLP tasks: word sense disambiguation, sentiment analysis, and entity disambiguation. The results indicate that our approach successfully identifies the best-suited embeddings for these tasks, achieving an average improvement of 3.5% in accuracy compared to randomly selecting models from the same dataset.

This study investigates the characteristics of clusters within random geometric graphs, defined as a set of connected nodes distributed randomly within a bounded area. We introduce a specific metric for cluster "intensity," defined as the count of nodes per unit area. Our analysis demonstrates that for graphs generated by a random variable with a probability density function that is strictly positive and bounded on the unit square, the maximum possible intensity of a $k$-node cluster is bounded from above by a constant. This constant is a function of the specific density of the random variable and the specific cluster size $k$. We also prove that the probability of a cluster having intensity exceeding any given threshold diminishes exponentially as that threshold rises.

We introduce a novel method for deriving analytical solutions to Euler's equation of motion in terms of Lagrangian variables, applied to a rotating star. By employing a specific ansatz, we determine the velocity field and express the corresponding Lagrangian flow map.

The Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) spacetime serves as a spherically symmetric solution to Einstein's equations, representing inhomogeneous cosmology. This study investigates the analogous solution within Palatini $f(R)$ gravity, a theory where the metric varies but the connection remains independent. We establish the field equations for the Lemoître-Tolman-Bondi metric within this framework and derive the corresponding equations of motion. Additionally, we analyze the spacetime's causal structure and examine its physical implications.

We demonstrate that any $N$-particle quantum state defined on a $d$-dimensional space can be locally transformed into a state composed of block-diagonal subblocks, where each corresponds to a nonlocally quantum-correlated (NLQC) state. This finding implies that NLQC represents a universal phenomenon occurring in all dimensions for arbitrary multipartite systems. Furthermore, we establish that the NLQC property is robust against local noise, provided the noise intensity remains sufficiently low.

This study introduces a new approach for predicting user visual attention on web pages by leveraging gaze data analytics. The proposed method continuously forecasts attention levels for short intervals, specifically 100 milliseconds, by analyzing data from a limited window of 200 milliseconds. The core of this technique involves a dedicated data preprocessing step that segments raw gaze recordings into 200 ms windows and subsequently breaks each window into 100 ms segments for attention prediction. The system employs a Random Forest classifier to determine the attention level of each 100 ms segment, utilizing gaze-derived features extracted from the preceding 100 ms segment and the 100 ms context prior to the window's start. The model is trained on a dataset of 100 ms segments labeled with their specific attention levels. The study concludes with an evaluation of this prediction system's performance.

This paper introduces a novel transmission reconfigurable intelligent surface (TRIS) designed to manage the phase of signals passing through it. Unlike traditional reflective surfaces, TRIS enables transmissive phase control, offering a more flexible approach to signal manipulation. The authors present a TRIS prototype featuring 168 transmit elements, 168 corresponding phase shifters, and 168 control circuits, with each phase shifter implemented using a compact, low-cost, and low-loss PIN diode PIN-diod switch-based structure. The system's performance was evaluated through both simulations and experiments, with results indicating that the TRIS prototype successfully achieved the targeted phase control. The research further demonstrates the potential of TRIS technology to enhance the performance of sixth-generation (6G) communication systems.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) involves optimizing a policy within a fixed dataset, a scenario where the agent cannot explore new state-action pairs. While recent research has largely focused on linear function approximation in linear MDPs, this paper investigates the broader, more practical case of general linear function approximation. We propose a new linear programming (LP) framework for offline RL that leverages the dual relationship between LP formulations and offline RL. By utilizing the dual LP, we derive a sample complexity bound of $\widetilde{O}(d^2H^2/\epsilon)$, where $d$ represents the dimension of the linear span and $H$ is the episode length. This result is nearly optimal, matching the best-known lower bounds up to a logarithmic factor. Furthermore, our approach offers several advantages: it is conceptually straightforward, applies to general offline RL problems, and provides a unified proof technique that recovers existing results from the literature.

We report the detection of a supermassive black hole (SMBH) in the galaxy J0437+2456, identified by the broad emission lines of C IV and Mg II. The broad C IV line exhibits a full width at half maximum (FWHM) of 10,000 km/s, while the Mg II line has an FWHM of 3,000 km/s. The ratio between these widths is approximately 3.3, which is significantly lower than the typical ratio of 6–7 observed in standard broad-line active galactic nuclei (AGN). This narrow width for the Mg II line suggests that the broad-line region (BLR) of this object is dominated by a slow, dense wind. Furthermore, the broad C IV line displays a pronounced blue asymmetry, a feature commonly associated with AGN outflows. This paper examines the planar three-body problem, focusing on sequences of collinear configurations. We demonstrate that if one body undergoes a collision within such a sequence, it must be followed either by another collision involving the same pair of bodies or by a different impact involving the remaining three masses.

Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) is a powerful technique for studying biological systems, offering high-contrast, quantitative, and non-destructive measurements of fluorophore environments. However, the resulting images are often blurred by the microscope's point spread function (PSF). This study introduces a deconvolution method to enhance FLIM image resolution. We developed a generalized framework for the linear deconvolution of FLIM data, which we validated using synthetic data and a real-world application involving the deconvolution of a cell stained with a fluorescent dye.

This study introduces a novel approach to personalized product search that leverages user behavior modeling via graph convolutions. By constructing a graph where nodes represent users and products, and edges signify interactions, the method captures complex user behaviors. Specifically, graph convolutions are employed to aggregate information from a user's neighbors, enabling the identification of similar users and products. This aggregation process enhances the accuracy of search result ranking. Experimental validation using the Alibaba Taobao dataset demonstrates that the proposed method outperforms existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Unsupervised graph embedding is a crucial technique for analyzing complex networks, yet existing methods often struggle with two key issues: the inability to capture high-order node relationships and the failure to account for node structural attributes. To address these limitations, we introduce a novel framework for unsupervised deep manifold attributed embedding (D-MAGE). This approach effectively models high-order relational structures by integrating node attributes into a unified manifold learning model. Specifically, D-MAGE utilizes a graph convolutional network (GCN) to capture high-order connections and employs a manifold regularizer to capture local structural patterns. Furthermore, we introduce a new attribute-based distance metric designed to enhance the graph's attributed characteristics. Extensive experiments on various unsupervised learning tasks demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.

This study introduces a two-stage genetic algorithm (GA) designed to optimize non-orthogonal sequences for use in grant-free massive connectivity scenarios. The GA's primary objective is to minimize the peak-to-average power ratio (PAPR) of these sequences, thereby enhancing signal detection performance and reducing the probability of error. The proposed framework operates in two distinct phases: the initial stage employs a multi-carrier modulation technique to generate non-orthogonal sequences, while the secondary stage utilizes a genetic algorithm to refine the modulation parameters, specifically the subcarrier and symbol allocations, with the goal of minimizing PAPR. Simulation results demonstrate that the GA-generated sequences exhibit lower PAPR values compared to those produced by existing methods. Furthermore, the study confirms that the GA successfully maintains a low collision rate, proving its effectiveness in facilitating grant-free massive connectivity.

This study introduces a novel signal acquisition method for Comba torial Neural Network Compression Sensing (CNNCS) that operates without knowledge of the encoder used in conventional acquisition systems. In CNNCS, an artificial neural network reconstructs signals from incomplete measurements, with the system trained using data generated by a specific signal generation model. Traditionally, this model relies on the Fourier matrix for signal generation and reconstruction, a choice that restricts its applicability to Fourier-based measurement setups. To overcome this limitation, we propose a blind CNNCS framework capable of recovering signals from various measurement types regardless of the specific encoder employed. The proposed architecture utilizes a signal generation component based on a Taylor series expansion, which does not depend on specific Fourier matrices. By leveraging this encoder-agnostic generation approach, our method enables the recovery of signals across diverse measurement configurations.

This paper introduces a new method for enhancing the robustness of deep neural networks by integrating adversarial training with random transformations. The approach involves applying random transformations to the input data and simultaneously generating adversarial perturbations on the transformed samples. This strategy is designed to minimize the model's sensitivity to input perturbations. We demonstrate that the degree of perturbation should vary based on the specific random transformation applied. Furthermore, we propose an additional technique to boost generalization capabilities by utilizing the combination of random transformations and perturbations as a regularization method. The proposed framework is evaluated across three benchmark datasets—CIFAR-10, SVHN, and ImageNet—using various random transformations. The results indicate that our method achieves state-of-the-art performance in both domain adaptation and robustness against adversarial attacks.

This paper establishes that on Jordan algebras consisting of matrix rings, local and 2-locating derivations are in fact identical to regular derivations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that local derivations on Jordan algebras of matrix rings, defined over commutative involutive rings, are central. Finally, we prove that for Jordan algebras of matrix rings where the underlying field has a characteristic not equal to 2, every 2-local derivation is also a local derivation.

The study of the gravitational lensing effect on a Dirac monopole in the Berry phase is presented. We examine the deflection angle for a monopole traversing the spacetime of a Schwarzschild black hole, as well as for a monopole moving through the background of a global monopole. Additionally, zeroth-order and first-order perturbation calculations for the deflection angle are performed for a monopole in the vicinity of a Kerr black hole.

This study examines the density dependence of the spin-orbit (SO) order parameter in Bose-Emin condensates, demonstrating that compact solitons can emerge when the SO coupling strength varies. These findings are corroborated by numerical simulations.

This paper investigates whether they constitute a spin-2 triplet pair by analyzing their decay patterns into $\Sigma(1385)\pi$ and $\Sigma(1660)\pi$ channels. The analysis reveals that the $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ exhibits a significantly stronger coupling to these decay channels compared to the $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$, indicating that the two states likely do not form a spin-2 doublet. Furthermore, the study examines the decay of the $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$ into $\Sigma(1660)\pi$ and $\Sigma(1660)\pi$ channels, finding that the $\Sigma(1660)\pi$ channel is more prominent than the $\Sigma(1660)\pi$ channel, which contradicts the expectation for a spin-2 doublet. This study examines the potential of future high-energy muon colliders for discovering axion-like particles (ALPs) and performing precision measurements of their interactions. We conduct a detailed analysis of the resonant production of ALPs via the Drell-Yan process, specifically investigating the impact of muon spin polarization on detection rates. Our findings indicate that muon spin polarization can significantly enhance the production cross-section, potentially increasing it by as much as an order of magnitude. Furthermore, we examine ALPs that couple to muons through derivative interactions and assess the feasibility of conducting high-precision studies of their properties. Our results demonstrate that such interactions can lead to distinctive, non-exponential decay time distributions, offering a unique avenue for probing ALP properties. Finally, we outline the potential for future high-precision investigations of these particles' masses, decay widths, and coupling strengths.

This paper introduces MetaSys, an open-source, practical framework designed to manage metadata for CPU architectures. By utilizing a centralized, in-memory repository, MetaSys enables seamless cross-layer optimizations, allowing software to dynamically access runtime architectural details. This capability facilitates the creation of more efficient software that can leverage hardware features, adapt to specific configurations, and scale effectively. The system is designed to be modular and flexible, supporting various metadata types, including those for memory hierarchy, cache, and branch prediction. Furthermore, it offers diverse interfaces for retrieving metadata, ranging from standard C APIs to high-level abstractions like C++ classes and Python functions. The discussion covers the implementation of this system, its deployment on real hardware, and an evaluation demonstrating its impact on software performance. Finally, the paper illustrates how MetaSys can enable cross-layer optimizations, using a software-aided adaptive branch prediction technique as a concrete example.

This paper introduces transfer learning strategies for image classification that leverage pre-trained deep neural networks and synthetic data. We introduce two novel approaches: the first employs a Siamese network architecture to learn from pairs of images, while the second utilizes synthetic data generated via GANs. Both methods are evaluated on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets. The Siamese-based scheme is assessed using a nearest neighbor classifier, whereas synthetic data is integrated into a deep neural network through contrastive loss. Experimental results indicate that the Siamese approach outperforms traditional fine-tuning on CIFAR-10, achieving a 2.5% improvement in accuracy, and matches the performance of fine-tuning on CIFAR-100. However, on CIFAR-10, the synthetic data-based scheme yields results comparable to fine-tuning, with both methods converging to a 90% accuracy.

This paper examines a class of inhomogeneous, anisotropic, and singular quasilinear elliptic systems featuring $p(x), q(x)$-growth and $p(x)-N$ constraints within the context of $R^N$. We establish the existence of weak solutions for this system. The proof strategy synthesizes the techniques outlined in [19] and [20] with a novel approach.

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are a cornerstone of deep learning for sequential data, yet they often struggle with capturing long-term dependencies. This challenge stems from the fact that, during training, gradients must traverse numerous time steps to reach earlier states, leading to vanishing or exploding gradients. This work introduces Fourier recurrent units (FRUs), a novel architecture designed to mitigate these vanishing gradient issues. By employing the Fourier series to model temporal dependencies, FRUs enable training gradients to propagate across long sequences, thereby facilitating the learning of long-term dependencies. Theoretical analysis confirms that FRUs can learn dependencies of arbitrary length. Furthermore, FRUs offer a computationally efficient alternative to existing solutions, such as hypernetworks and LSTMs, for modeling long-term patterns. Experimental results across various tasks demonstrate that FRUs achieve superior performance in learning long-term dependencies compared to standard RNN variants.

This paper investigates the problem of identifying the optimal policy in Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) by comparing the cumulative rewards of two distinct policies. We introduce a novel class of MDPs defined by a specific state structure, termed "navigation MDPs," in which the agent's primary objective is to locate the superior policy. We analyze the sample complexity required to determine the best approach with high confidence, demonstrating that the required number of samples scales with the size of the state space for navigation MDPs, contrasting with the sample complexity of general MDPs, which depends on the size of the action space. Additionally, we propose a new algorithm called Navigation, which leverages pairwise comparisons to determine the best policy with high confidence. We establish a theoretical upper bound on the sample complexity of the Navigation algorithm and validate its efficacy through experiments on navigation MDPs and the extended version of the Taxi domain.

We introduce a novel dual-wake injection method for producing high-brightness, linearly polarized attosecond electron bunches. This approach employs a short, high-amplitude laser pulse to generate a plasma wakefield, creating an initial electron bunch that is subsequently injected into a second, longer laser pulse. This second interaction establishes a strong longitudinal electric field within the bunch, inducing a spin-flip transition that results in a highly polarized state. The resulting electron beam possesses a normalized emittance of $10^{-9}$ m rad, a duration of 250 attoseconds, and a beam current of 100 microamperes. The generated pulses are intrinsically linearly polarized along the direction of the external field, with polarization degrees exceeding 90%. Furthermore, the proposed technique is scalable, offering the potential to produce electron bunches with energies reaching up to 100 MeV.

We examine astrophysical factors influencing life, with a particular focus on the emergence and evolution of complexity. Our analysis reveals that the rate at which complexity arises is governed by the fundamental laws of thermodynamics. Consequently, astrophysical conditions dictate the upper limit of available free energy, thereby establishing a theoretical ceiling for the speed of evolutionary development.

This study examines the advantages and limitations of utilizing web-based data and AI for evidence-based R&D policy-making concerning climate change. By analyzing data from the OpenAlex API, we mapped the global landscape of climate change research, specifically focusing on the United States and China. Our findings indicate that web-based data offers a cost-effective and timely method for monitoring research landscapes, particularly when combined with AI-driven tools. However, the approach faces significant challenges: the sheer volume of data is difficult to process, and the data's inherent bias limits its utility for comparative analysis. Consequently, while useful for tracking individual institutions, the data is less effective for analyzing the broader national research ecosystem.

Android's dominance in the mobile market has spurred research into securing its platform, with side-channel analysis emerging as a critical area of study. Although recent efforts have focused on Android's Java Virtual Machine (JVM), the application of side-channel analysis to the Native Distribution Kit (NDK) remains largely unexplored. This paper introduces ASVAAN, a semi-automated tool designed to detect side-channel leaks in NDK C/C++ applications. By employing a template-based methodology, ASVAAN automatically generates and analyzes code templates to identify vulnerabilities. The tool was evaluated using 10 open-source NDK applications, with results demonstrating that ASVAAN successfully uncovered side-channel leaks in 7 of the tested apps.

Blockchain technology has gained significant traction for facilitating secure, decentralized, and transparent transactions. Ethereum, a prominent blockchain platform, serves as a decentralized, open-source, and programmable network designed to support various applications. This study analyzes the temporal dynamics of Ethereum's ego networks, specifically examining connections between self-interested individuals and their associated transactions. We categorize these networks based on specific transaction types, such as transfers, smart contracts, and token activities, to evaluate how their structural properties evolve over time. Our findings indicate that while the networks' size and clustering coefficients remain relatively stable, their path lengths fluctuate. Additionally, we observe that the networks exhibit a small-world structure, with both clustering and transitivity coefficients being notably high.

We report on the observation of quantum oscillations in a two-dimensional electron system (2DES) located at the LaAlO$_3$/SrTiO$_3$ interface, achieved via optical excitation of the associated excitonic resonance. This study investigates the temperature dependence of the oscillations and demonstrates that they persist down to approximately 10 K. Furthermore, we observe a significant suppression of the quantum oscillation amplitude when optical excitation is absent. These findings indicate that the exciton enhances the oscillation amplitude by elevating the electron temperature and diminishing electron-phonon scattering rates.

This paper examines the inherent complexity of cut-elimination and resolution within Pomset logic, which extends Brouwer–Heyting–Bodmer logic with the mix rule. We demonstrate that Pomset logic functions as a robust system for Brouwer–Heyting–Bodmer logic, enabling the simulation of mix-dependent reductions in Brouwer–Heyting–Bodmer logic, and thus achieving the same level of complexity. We further prove that polynomial-time many-one reductions can be applied to cut-elimination in both systems, confirming their equivalent complexity.

The Gaudin model, characterized by a family of integrable systems, is defined by an algebra known as Ding-Iohara-Miki. Within this framework, the Gaudin operators are represented by the generators of Ding-Iohara-Miki. This work investigates penton identities within the Ding-Iohara-Miki algebra and derives corresponding penton relations for the operators constituting the Ding-Iohara-Miki representation of the quantum affine algebra of type A.
